description: A real, public curl security advisory (CVE-2026-92391), checked at its last affected version. Its claims are true and must never be CONTRADICTED (rule 1). The recursion runs through a function pointer, so a static call graph won't find it; CANT_CHECK is then an acceptable miss. Fixed in 8.23.0 by commit d7546809d5 ("mime: do curl_mime_free() non-recursively").

report.title: curl_mime_free stack overflow by recursion
report.body:
Affected versions: libcurl 7.56.0 up to and including 8.22.0.

A deeply nested multipart MIME structure constructed via the public API causes
a stack overflow in libcurl during normal cleanup operations. An excessive
recursion depth within `curl_mime_free` leads to unbounded stack frame
allocation during structure traversal, ultimately crashing the host process.

claim.statement: curl_mime_free is a function in libcurl

evidence.note: The real implementation. An empty stub at line 2190 is used only when MIME support is compiled out.
Hop 1, inside curl_mime_free (line 1113): free each part.
Hop 3, inside cleanup_part_content (line 1056): a call through a function pointer.
Inside Curl_mime_set_subparts (line 1468): for a part holding nested subparts, the pointer is set to mime_subparts_free.
The public curl_mime_subparts (line 1519) passes take_ownership = TRUE, so nesting via the public API takes that branch.
Hop 4, inside mime_subparts_free (line 1075): back into curl_mime_free, once per nesting level.
